sources.entry: Shhh - Keep secrets out of emails or chat logs, share them using secure links with passphrase and expiration dates. MIT Python

summary.one_liner: Shhh is a small Flask web app that creates encrypted, passphrase-protected, self-destructing links for sharing secrets so they stay out of emails and chat logs.
summary.what_it_does: The sender sets an expiration date and a passphrase, and Shhh generates a unique link to share with the receiver alongside the passphrase. Secrets are encrypted with Fernet using a password, a random salt and 100,000 iterations, and the passphrases are not stored. A secret is permanently deleted from the database when its expiration date passes, when the receiver decrypts it, or when the number of failed open attempts is exceeded. The README also mentions an API, a Heroku one-click deploy option, and Docker-based development setup with PostgreSQL or MySQL plus Adminer. A separate Go command-line client, shhh-cli, is mentioned. Secret length is configurable, defaulting to 250 characters.
use_cases: Sharing passwords with a colleague without putting them in email
Sending one-time sensitive text with an expiring link
Self-hosting a private secret-sharing service for an organisation
Passing credentials through chat without leaving them in chat logs
Deploying a secret-sharing app to Heroku
notable: Secrets are encrypted and deleted after expiry, first successful read, or too many attempts
Includes a REST API and a separate Go CLI client (shhh-cli)
caveats: The project is being sunset in favor of secretapi, according to the README
The hosted public instance is temporarily unavailable, so self-hosting is needed
Docker setup and environment files are described as for development only, not production
